pdf_p1_excerpt: A Uniﬁed Framework for Generalized Moment Problems: a Novel Primal-Dual Approach Jiayi Guo, Simai He, Bo Jiang, Zhen Wang School of Information Management and Engineering, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, China, 200433, guo.jiayi@sufe.edu.cn, simaihe@mail.shufe.edu.cn, isyebojiang@gmail.com, zhenwang@163.sufe.edu.cn Generalized moment problems optimize functional expectation over a class of distributions with general- ized moment constraints, i.e., the function in the moment can be any measurable function. These problems2022 Jan have recently attracted growing interest due to their great ﬂexibility in representing nonstandard moment constraints, such as geometry-mean constraints, entropy constraints, and exponential-type moment con- 11 straints. Despite the increasing research interest, analytical solutions are mostly missing for these problems, and researchers have to settle for nontight bounds or numerical approaches that are either suboptimal or only applicable to some special cases. In addition, the techniques used to develop closed-form solutions to the standard moment problems are tailored for speciﬁc problem structures. In this paper, we propose a framework that provides a uniﬁed treatment for any moment problem. The key ingredient of the frame-[math.OC] work is a novel primal-dual optimality condition. This optimality condition enables us to reduce the original inﬁnite dimensional problem to a nonlinear equation system with a ﬁnite number of variables. In solving three speciﬁc moment problems, the framework demonstrates a clear path for identifying the analytical solution if one is available, otherwise, it produces semi-analytical solutions that lead to eﬃcient numerical algorithms. Finally, through numerical experiments, we provide further evidence regarding the performance of the resulting algorithms by solving a moment problem and a distributionally robust newsvendor problem. Key words : Distributionally robust optimization, Generalized moment problem, Newsvendor, Primal-dualarXiv:2201.01445v3 1. Introduction The generalized moment problem (see, e.g., Bertsimas and Popescu 2005) aims to optimize the expectation of a measurable function g(·) with general distributional moment information E[hi(X)] = mi for i = 1,...,n, where hi(·) can be any measurable function. The study of this prob- lem dates back to the pioneering work of Chebyshev (1874) and Markov (1884) on the standard moment problem (i.e., hi(X) = Xi). proof_map.claim: For the generalized moment problem (GMP) and its dual (DGMP) as formulated in §2, assuming strong duality and optimal primal/dual solutions, the stated certificate comprises p≥0 and global dual feasibility H(x;z)≥0 on Ω; primal moment feasibility; complementary slackness; and tangent equalities at every differentiable interior support point. These conditions are necessary and sufficient for the given primal distribution and dual vector to be optimal.
proof_map.location: PDF pp.7–10, (GMP)/(DGMP), (PriCond), (SlackCond), (TagntCond), Theorem 1 and proof, esp. p.9.
conditions: strong duality is explicitly assumed for the iff theorem
global dual feasibility must hold on all of Ω, not just at support points
tangency is imposed only at differentiable interior support points; nondifferentiable or boundary support points need not satisfy it
attainment of the displayed primal/dual candidates is part of the statement that such optimal solutions exist

proof_map.claim: The proposed three-step approach uses the optimality conditions to identify a rough optimal-support pattern, derive an analytical or semi-analytical support candidate from the finite nonlinear system, then verify probability/moment feasibility and global dual feasibility. It is a candidate-generation plus certificate-verification workflow, not a general guaranteed numerical algorithm for every measurable generalized moment problem.
